slots.brief: Show a rectangular loop entering/exiting a uniform B-field region at constant speed; give induced emf as a function of time and ask for a specific value (or the emf at a given position) using flux change over time.

slots.subtopic: Magnetic field due to finite wire / polygon loop
slots.brief: Superposition of magnetic fields at the centre of a regular polygon (or a combination of two finite wires/loops); no figure, ask the net B and its direction.
Show a block released from rest on top of a frictionless incline that compresses a spring at the bottom; ask the maximum compression using conservation of mechanical energy.
Give a particle's position vector and angular velocity (or force) in component form and ask for the torque/angular momentum vector using the cross product.
A sample's activity drops to a given fraction after some time; ask how many half-lives elapsed, or find the time for activity to drop by a stated factor.

slots.subtopic: Interference – mirror images as coherent sources
slots.brief: Show a Lloyd's-mirror / two-source setup (or reflected ray acting as a virtual coherent source); ask the path difference and whether the central/reflecting-surface point is bright or dark.
For a hydrogen-like ion or a transition between two given levels, ask the ratio of energies/radii/velocities between two states using Bohr-model formulas.
Compare elongation or breaking condition of two wires of same material but different lengths/radii under the same load; ask the ratio of elongations using Young's modulus.
Show a person walking on / jumping off a freely rotating platform (or a disc dropping onto another); use angular momentum conservation about the axis to find the new angular speed.
Show a wavefront diagram (spherical/plane) and ask which Huygens' principle statement correctly explains wavefront propagation / secondary wavelets.
A mirror forms an image with given object distance and magnification (or find image position); apply the mirror formula with sign conventions.
For a series LCR circuit at a given frequency, compute the impedance and the phase angle between voltage and current; ask whether the current leads or lags.
Given V as a function of position (e.g. V = kx² or ax + bx²), find the electric field (and ask for its value or zero point) by differentiating the potential.
Show a network of resistors (possibly with a Wheatstone-bridge-like arrangement) and ask the equivalent resistance between two terminals; simplify step by step.
Show a circuit of two or three logic gates fed by given inputs; ask the final Boolean output or to identify the equivalent single gate.
Given an EM wave's electric field amplitude, ask the ratio/relations between E₀, B₀ and intensity, or find the average energy density using E = cB.
Use R = ρL/A with volume conserved: a wire is stretched to n times its length; ask the factor by which resistance increases.
For a satellite in circular orbit, express its total energy / orbital speed in terms of the planet's mass and orbital radius; ask for the value or a symbolic expression.
Give y(x,t) = A sin(kx − ωt + φ) and ask for amplitude, wavelength, frequency and wave speed by matching with the standard form.
Show a dip circle / place with given horizontal and vertical components (or dip angle); use tan(dip) = Bv/Bh to find a missing component or the total field.
A body released/thrown vertically under gravity (or distance travelled in the nth second); use one kinematic equation to find time, speed or distance.
An ideal gas undergoes an isothermal/isobaric/isochoric change; use the first law to find heat supplied, work done or ΔU for given state changes.
Two rods of different materials/lengths/diameters joined or compared with same temperature difference; find the ratio of thermal conductances/heat flows.
Use Gauss's law with a symmetric surface (sphere/cylinder) to find the field at a given distance; test whether students can set up the correct Gaussian surface.
A current-carrying coil of given turns, area and current: compute its magnetic moment, and possibly the torque in a given field.
A charged capacitor is connected to an uncharged one; ask the fraction of initial energy lost as heat using charge sharing.
Two bodies thrown/projected (e.g. one from a cliff, another upward) meet after a given time; set up two equations and solve for the unknown speed or time.
A physical equation is proposed with an unknown constant X; find the dimensional formula of X (or check which quantity it could be) from dimensional consistency.

slots.chapter: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter
slots.brief: Show a photoelectric setup graph (stopping potential vs frequency or photocurrent vs voltage); use Einstein's equation to compare two metals or find work function and threshold frequency.
Two blocks connected by a string over a pulley (or stacked with friction between them); draw free-body equations and solve the acceleration and tension.
Give a truth table of outputs for a two/three-input combination; ask which gate arrangement (NAND/NOR wiring) reproduces it.
Compare rms speeds of two gases at the same/specified temperatures using v_rms ∝ √(T/M); find the ratio or the unknown temperature.
Give a wave on a string as a function and ask the maximum particle velocity (or ratio of particle velocity to wave velocity) using SHM of the medium element.
Show a solid floating at an interface between two immiscible liquids (or partly immersed); use density balance to find the fraction immersed in each liquid.
Given a planet's mean density, express surface gravity g in terms of density and radius (or compare two planets); one substitution.
Show x(t) or v(t) graphs of several candidates and identify which represents SHM, or read off amplitude/frequency/phase from a given SHM curve.

slots.chapter: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter
slots.subtopic: de Broglie wavelength of accelerated particles
slots.brief: Find the de Broglie wavelength of an electron (or alpha particle) accelerated through a given potential difference using λ = h/√(2meV).
Two/three concurrent forces in equilibrium with one unknown force magnitude or angle; resolve into components and solve.
Compare curie and becquerel / relate activity in curies to decays per second, or convert between radioactivity units; one-step unit conversion.
For an astronomical telescope, given objective and eyepiece focal lengths (and tube length), compute the magnification; one formula, sign conventions.
Give wavelength of electromagnetic radiation; ask energy of one photon and of one mole of photons in kJ.
Provide structures of three alkyl/benzyl halides in a figure; rank their rates of solvolysis (SN1) and justify via carbocation stability.
Show a plot of log[A] vs t (or ln[A] vs t) for a first-order reaction in a figure; ask what the slope equals (–k/2.303 or –k) or extract k from the slope.
Which statement about ozone depletion is incorrect (e.g. role of CFCs, Cl radical chain, NO catalysis)?
At hard difficulty: ask about zwitterion behaviour and pH-dependent charge of amino acids with acidic/basic side chains, or which amino acid lacks a chiral centre.
Conceptual: in the Freundlich isotherm x/m = k·P^(1/n), what happens to adsorption as pressure increases (and significance of n > 1) — statement-based recall.
Give percentage composition of a compound; ask for empirical formula, then molecular formula given molar mass.
For XeF2/XeF4/XeF6, ask hybridisation and geometry (or number of lone pairs); e.g. shape of XeF4 with bond angles.
Which class does a named drug belong to (e.g. equanil/veronal – tranquilizer; aspirin – analgesic)?

slots.subtopic: Diagonal relationship of Li and Mg
slots.brief: Which statement about the Li–Mg diagonal relationship is correct/incorrect (similar ionic size, nitride formation, carbonate decomposition)?
Alkyl halide + Mg in dry ether followed by reaction with a carbonyl and hydrolysis — identify the final alcohol product.
In a spinel or ionic solid of fcc oxide ions with ions in tetrahedral/octahedral voids, determine the fraction of voids occupied and hence the formula.
Which amine (primary/secondary/tertiary) gives a foul smell with chloroform and KOH, and identify the product formed.
Ratio of wavelengths (or energies) of first line of Balmer vs Lyman series for H, or compare H vs He+ transition energies.
Give two octahedral complexes (one with weak-field, one with strong-field ligand); compare unpaired electrons and spin-only magnetic moments.
Identify Lucas reagent and how it distinguishes 1°, 2°, 3° alcohols by turbidity appearance time.
Which of the given orderings across electronegativity, electron gain enthalpy and ionisation enthalpy (including anomalies like Cl > F, O vs S) is incorrect?
Show reaction scheme in figure: aldehyde lacking α-H with concentrated NaOH giving alcohol + salt; identify the reaction and products.
For a balanced gas-phase reaction (e.g. combustion), compute Δn_g and convert between ΔH and ΔU at temperature T.
Given Kc and temperature for a gaseous equilibrium, calculate Kp (or ask for which reaction Kp = Kc).
Given a substituted benzene (two groups with conflicting directives) in a figure, predict the major monosubstitution product.
Use given reaction enthalpies (or mean bond enthalpies) to compute ΔH of a target reaction via Hess's law cycle.
Why are Zn2+, Sc3+ or Cu+ salts colourless while Cu2+ is blue — d-d transitions and d-electron count.
Asymmetric ether reacted with excess vs one equivalent HI — give the products in each case and note SN1 vs SN2 pathway.
Assign R/S to two or three Fischer projections of the same stereocentre; identify identical/enantiomeric pairs or rank by configuration.
Given initial amount and fraction remaining after time t, find the half-life (or time for N half-lives) using count-half-lives logic.
Structure of an alkene (di-substituted, in figure) undergoes ozonolysis with Zn/H2O; identify the carbonyl fragments formed.
Which alkyl halide and alkoxide combination gives the best yield of a specified ether via Williamson synthesis (avoid 3° halides)?
Given a complex like Co(NH3)5Br(SO4), identify the type of isomerism (ionisation/hydrate/linkage) and which pairs actually show it.
Given limiting molar conductivities of two strong electrolytes, compute Λ°m of a weak electrolyte (e.g. CH3COOH from NaCl, HCl, CH3COONa).

At hard difficulty: a sparingly soluble salt/solute association-dissociation problem combining depression in freezing point or osmotic pressure with computing i and degree of dissociation/association from data.
For PCl5 ⇌ PCl3 + Cl2 at total equilibrium pressure P and degree of dissociation α, derive Kp; numerical with given α or given Kp to find α.
Compute density of a gas at given T and P using d = PM/RT, or compare effusion/density ratio of two gases.
Why does H2O have abnormally high boiling point compared to H2S — explain via intermolecular hydrogen bonding (statement/one-liner).
Give formulae of 3–4 molecules (e.g. SF4, ClF3, NH3, XeF4); identify shapes/hybridisation and match to given geometry list.
For a lanthanide ion (e.g. Eu3+/Gd3+), write the 4f configuration and calculate the magnetic moment using √n(n+2) BM or discuss orbital contribution.
Given E°cell, compute ΔG° and Kc for the cell reaction using ΔG° = –nFE° = –RT ln K; two-step numeric.
Arrange given alkyl/benzyl/allyl radicals in order of stability with reasoning on hyperconjugation and resonance; pick the correct series from options.
What happens when diborane reacts with water/CO/O2 or Lewis bases like NH3 at different temperatures; identify products (e.g. B2H6 + 6H2O → 2H3BO3 + 6H2).
Match vitamins (A, B, C, D, K) with their deficiency diseases or classify as fat/water soluble.
Give a moderately common descriptive word (e.g., 'meticulous') in a short context sentence and ask for the closest synonym among four options.
Write a sentence with a collective noun or 'one of the...' construction where the verb disagrees; ask which part contains the error.
Pick an abstract adjective (e.g., 'ephemeral') presented as 'Choose the word nearest in meaning to...' with four plausible distractors.
Use an everyday idiom like 'to let the cat out of the bag' in a simple sentence and ask for its meaning; distractors should be literal interpretations.
Simple sentence with a blank testing a fixed prepositional pair (e.g., 'devoid ___', 'comply ___'), with three wrong prepositions as options.

slots.subtopic: Para jumble with given first sentence
slots.brief: Four short jumbled sentences on a simple everyday topic with the opening sentence given; student orders the rest using pronoun and connector clues.
Give a moderate word like 'candid' and ask for the nearest opposite; ensure one option is a synonym trap.

slots.subtopic: Sentence completion with double blanks (high-level vocabulary)
slots.brief: Hard sentence with two blanks requiring contrasting tone words (e.g., skeptic/credulous pair); options are word pairs, and pairs must be internally coherent.
Simple friendly sentence with one blank (e.g., 'She was ___ by the good news') and four common words, only one fitting the tone.

slots.subtopic: Mixed error spotting with 'no error' option
slots.brief: Long, subtle sentence involving tense shift and gerund after preposition where everything is actually correct; the trap is that students wrongly mark a correct part.

slots.subtopic: Tense consistency (simple past vs present perfect)
slots.brief: Give a sentence where present perfect is misused with a finished-time marker ('yesterday'); ask for the corrected version among four rewrites.

slots.subtopic: PQRS jumbled parts of a coherent paragraph
slots.brief: Four labeled parts (P, Q, R, S) of a medium paragraph on an academic topic, with clear pronoun-reference and logical sequence clues; ask for the correct PQRS order.
Medium analogy pair (e.g., 'garrulous : talkative :: X : Y') testing synonym/antonym or part-whole relationships; distractor pairs should shift the relation type.
Give four similar-looking words; ask which one comes first (or last) in a dictionary order.
Pair like ABC : DEF, then ask analogous pair for another letter group with a positional shift pattern.
Two statements with all/some quantifiers; ask which conclusions definitely follow.
Four words, three share a category; pick the one that does not belong.
Persons in a row with position clues from both ends; ask who is in the middle / how many are between two people.
Mixed letter-number series where letters shift and numbers follow arithmetic pattern; find the missing term.
A word is coded using a positional-value rule; apply same rule to a new word to get the code.
Pointing-to-person chain with phrases like 'he is the son of my father's sister'; identify exact relation.
Give the general equation of a circle with messy coefficients; ask for its centre and radius via completing the square.
Two lines in symmetric form; decide whether they intersect, are parallel or skew by comparing direction ratios and checking coplanarity.
Area bounded between a parabola and a line; set up intersection points and integrate with respect to y for cleaner limits.
Given a complex equation of the form |z - a| = k|z - b| or similar, solve using |z|² = z·z̄ to land on a real linear equation in x and y.
Simple trigonometric equation reducible to sin = 0 or cos = 0 form; ask for the general solution set.
Limit of the form (sin ax)/(tan bx) or 1-cos(kx) over x² as x→0; direct standard-limit substitution.
Arrange letters of a word with repeated letters under a block condition (e.g., all vowels together or two specific letters never adjacent), using total minus invalid.
y = product/quotient of trig functions of 2x; simplify using identities before differentiating, then evaluate derivative at a specific angle.
Find the equation of a line through the intersection point of two given lines and satisfying an extra condition (passing through a given point or parallel to a given line).
Given a small square matrix A, compute a higher power like A⁵ or Aⁿ using a pattern or a relation like A² = kA, then read off a requested entry.
If α, β are roots of a quadratic, find a symmetric expression (e.g., α² + β² or α³ + β³) in terms of coefficients via Vieta.
Ungrouped data set of 5-7 numbers; compute the mean and the variance/standard deviation directly from definitions.
Point given in 3D; find its perpendicular distance from a coordinate axis (say the y-axis) using the formula √(x² + z²).
Simplify an expression of the form 1/(a + bi) or a fraction of complex numbers by multiplying with conjugate; express result in standard form.
Find the equation of a parabola with vertex at origin given its focus or directrix (axis along a coordinate axis); identify the equation from the focus.
Definite integral of an odd/even function over a symmetric interval, possibly combined with a known definite-integral property like ∫f(x)dx = ∫f(a+b-x)dx to simplify before evaluating.
Small set of 2D vectors with given magnitudes; use a dot-product identity (|a+b|² or |a-b|²) to find an unknown dot product or the angle.
Line of the form y = mx + c touches a given circle; impose the perpendicular-distance-equals-radius (or c² = a²(1+m²)) condition and solve for the parameter.
3×3 determinant with expressions in x and trigonometric values in rows/columns; use row/column operations to factor the determinant and show it equals zero for specific values.
Evaluate a composite like sin⁻¹(something) or tan⁻¹x + tan⁻¹y using the standard identity for the sum/difference of inverse tangents, checking the principal-value branch.
Use differentials to approximate the value of a root/surd like √(26) or cube root of a nearby perfect number; compute the error estimate dy.
A linear programming word problem (diet/production); formulate constraints, plot the feasible region corners and maximise the objective function at a corner point.
A dataset is transformed (each value multiplied by a constant and/or a constant added); state the new mean and variance without recomputation, using transformation properties.
Solve a first-order linear ODE dy/dx + P(x)y = Q(x) where P is a simple function (e.g., 1/x or a constant) via the integrating factor; possibly with an initial condition.
Find the domain of a function involving a square root and a denominator (e.g., √(polynomial)/(rational expression)); intersect the positivity condition with the denominator-nonzero condition.
Definite integral requiring integration by parts (e.g., ∫x·eˣ or ∫x·sin x over limits); apply the parts formula and evaluate boundary terms.
Given a polynomial/cubic, determine the intervals on which it is increasing and decreasing by studying the sign chart of f'(x).
Area common to two circles (or between a circle and a parabola) using symmetry: find intersection points, set up the integral over half the region and double it.
Form 3-digit (or 4-digit) numbers from a given multiset of digits satisfying a divisibility or digit-position restriction; count case by case (e.g., by last digit).
Two events with given individual probabilities and independence/intersection; compute P(A|B) or check whether A and B are independent using the definition.
Find the coefficient of a specific power of x (e.g., x³ or 1/x) in a binomial expansion by setting up the general term and solving for r.

slots.subtopic: Perpendicular distance from point to line
slots.brief: 3D line in vector/cartesian form and an external point; find the coordinates of the foot of the perpendicular and the shortest distance from the point to the line.
Give two relations on a small set (shown via a diagram of ordered pairs/arrows); decide which standard properties (reflexive, symmetric, transitive) each relation satisfies.
Sum of a series whose general term splits by telescoping (e.g., 1/(n(n+1)) or similar partial-fraction pattern); find the sum to n terms or infinite sum.
Binomial-type scenario (e.g., coins/dice with p given) with a stated condition such as exactly k successes being a given value or a mean; recover the unknown parameter n or p.
A two-parameter family of curves (parabolas/circles) is given; form the differential equation by differentiating and eliminating the arbitrary constants.
Sum of coefficients or a weighted binomial coefficient sum (e.g., r·nCr terms) obtained by differentiating (1+x)ⁿ or substituting x = 1, x = -1.
Count functions between two small finite sets with a given property (e.g., number of onto functions from a k-element set to an m-element set) via inclusion-exclusion.
Given position vectors of triangle vertices, classify the triangle (right-angled/isosceles/scalene) by computing side lengths via dot/cross products.
Find the inverse of a given 2×2 (or small 3×3) matrix using the adjoint divided by the determinant; verify by multiplying with the original.

slots.subtopic: Image of a point in a line
slots.brief: Find the image of a point in a given line (or equivalently the mirror image of a point across a line): use the perpendicular-foot construction and double it.

slots.subtopic: Range of a sin + b cos
slots.brief: Find the range or maximum/minimum of an expression of the form a sin θ + b cos θ + c using the amplitude bound √(a² + b²).
A limit at a point where the expression involves |x| or a greatest-integer/greatest-modulus piece; evaluate left and right limits separately and match, or conclude the limit does not exist.
Given a small set and a proposed function/rule (or two subsets shown via a simple Venn description), verify properties or compute the inverse mapping / number of elements in a region.
Indefinite integral of the form ∫f(ax + b)dx or ∫x·√(quadratic)dx solvable by a simple substitution; carry out the substitution and back-substitute.
